---
title: "Set Up Your Computer"
---

The course is made to be done on your own computer. The notebooks build on each other: one notebook saves a file or a model, and a later notebook uses it. A local setup keeps all of that in one place. It takes about 15 minutes.

You install three tools:

- **Git**, to download the course and get updates;
- **uv**, which installs the right Python version (3.13) and every package the course uses. You don't need to install Python yourself;
- **VS Code**, the editor in which you open and run the notebooks.

Everything together needs about 3 GB of disk space: the course environment (about 0.7 GB on macOS, about 1.5 GB on Linux, where XGBoost also installs GPU libraries) and uv's download cache, which you can empty afterwards with `uv cache clean`.

## 1. Install Git

Download Git from [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/downloads) and install it. On macOS, Git is often already there. Check it in a terminal (on Windows: PowerShell):

```bash
git --version
```

## 2. Install uv

macOS and Linux:

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

Windows (PowerShell):

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
```

Close and reopen your terminal, then check that it works:

```bash
uv --version
```

Other ways to install uv are in the [uv documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/).

## 3. Download the course

Go to the folder where you keep your projects, then:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/BredaUniversityADSAI/introduction-to-ml.git
cd introduction-to-ml
```

## 4. Install Python and the packages

From the `introduction-to-ml` folder:

```bash
uv sync
```

The first time, this downloads Python 3.13 and all packages into a `.venv` folder inside the course folder. That takes a few minutes. Nothing is installed elsewhere on your computer.

## 5. Check that it works

```bash
uv run python -c "import sklearn, rdkit, xgboost, lightgbm; print('All set')"
```

If you see `All set`, you are ready. On macOS, if this fails with a message about `libomp`, install the OpenMP runtime with [Homebrew](https://brew.sh/) and try again:

```bash
brew install libomp
```

## 6. Open the course in VS Code

Download VS Code from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com/) and install it. Then:

1. Open the course folder ("File" > "Open Folder…", then choose `introduction-to-ml`).
2. VS Code offers to install the extensions the course recommends: Python and Jupyter, which run the notebooks, and Quarto (optional). Install them.
3. Open a notebook, click "Select Kernel" in the top right and choose the `.venv` environment.

In the Explorer on the left you see the course as folders, one per Self-study theme and one per DataLab iteration, with the files numbered in the order you work through them. See [Jupyter notebooks in VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/datascience/jupyter-notebooks) for more about working with notebooks.

## 7. Check the notebooks

Open `self-study/theme-1/02_getting_started.ipynb` and run all cells. If they run without errors, you are ready to start. In any notebook, this cell shows which Python it uses and the folder it runs in:

```python
import sys
from pathlib import Path
print(sys.executable)  # should be inside the course's .venv folder
print(Path.cwd())      # the folder of the notebook
```

The notebooks read the data with paths relative to their own folder: a DataLab notebook in `datalab/iteration-2/` reads `../../data/...`. Files you create (such as the processed CSV files) go in `data/002_processed_data/`, models in `models/`.

## What is where

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `self-study/` | Self-study, one folder per theme: the notebooks and the reading pages you see on this website |
| `datalab/` | DataLab, one folder per iteration: the notebooks and the pages you see on this website |
| `data/` | All datasets of the project (see `data/README.md`) |
| `models/` | Models you save while working through the notebooks |
| `tools/` | The scorer for your test-set predictions (`score.py`) |

In each theme and iteration folder, the files are numbered in the order of this website, starting with the overview page `00_overview.qmd`. Follow the [course route](course-guide.qmd#the-course-route): it takes you through Self-study and DataLab in turn. The `.qmd` files are the pages of this website: read them here, where the figures, videos and interactive parts work. The notebooks (`.ipynb`) are the files you open and run.

## Getting updates

The course is an early release and still changes. To get the latest version:

```bash
git pull
uv sync
```

`git pull` refuses to overwrite notebooks you have changed. The simplest way to avoid that: work in a copy of each notebook (for example `04_regression_mine.ipynb`), and keep the originals untouched. The files you create in `data/002_processed_data/` and `models/` are ignored by Git, so they never get in the way of an update.

## If something goes wrong

- **`uv` or `git`: command not found.** Close and reopen the terminal after installing. On Windows, use PowerShell.
- **A package is missing or behaves strangely.** Delete the `.venv` folder and run `uv sync` again.
- **`ModuleNotFoundError` in a notebook, although the check above printed `All set`.** The notebook runs in another Python. Click the kernel name in the top right of the notebook and choose the `.venv` environment.
- **`FileNotFoundError` for a data file.** Print `Path.cwd()` (see step 7) and check the path relative to that folder. If the missing file is `HOPV_homolumo_processed.csv` or `xy_df_hopv.csv`, an earlier notebook hasn't saved it yet: each Iteration 2 and 3 notebook says at the top which files it needs and which notebook creates them.
- **You want an extra package.** Run `uv add <package-name>` in the course folder and restart the notebook kernel. Don't use `pip install` inside a notebook: the package is lost at the next `uv sync`. Note that `uv add` changes `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, which can make a later `git pull` complain about these files.
- **Do not upgrade `rdkit`.** It is pinned to version 2025.9.3 on purpose: other versions compute some molecular descriptors differently from the course data.
- Still stuck? Ask in the course [Discussions](https://github.com/BredaUniversityADSAI/introduction-to-ml/discussions/categories/q-a). Say which operating system you use and paste the full error message.

## Only a quick look? Google Colab

Every notebook page on this website has an **Open in Colab** button. Colab runs the notebook in your browser, without installing anything, and the notebooks show how to load the data there. It is fine for a quick look or a single notebook. For the whole course, use the local setup: Colab forgets the files you create when the session ends, and the DataLab notebooks depend on files from earlier notebooks. If you still continue a DataLab notebook chain in Colab, download the files a notebook creates before the session ends, and upload them at the start of the next one.
